Subject: Post-call: sensitive header filtering & request/response log handling

Hi Amit —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side on the logging/redaction items we discussed:

Summary of needs you mentioned
- Request/response logs (API payloads) may contain patient identifiers (names, MRN, phone/email) and sensitive headers (Authorization/Trace-ID/session_cookie).
- Retention target: prefer 30 days for request traces, with an option to push to 7 days for high-sensitivity routes.
- Data residency: must remain in us-west-2 for the pilot.
- Auditability: security team needs a way to verify redaction rules and see proof of processing (not raw PII).

What we can provide (short):
- Two redaction modes: suppression (remove header/value) or deterministic hashing (HMAC) per header.
- Regex-based request/response scrubbing with policy profiles per route.
- Trace-ID handling: option to strip full trace IDs from logs while preserving a salted hash so we can correlate without exposing the raw IDs.
- Retention controls per log stream + export to customer-controlled S3 if you want to keep raw copies behind your KMS.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Can you share a small sample of anonymized request/response logs (redact patient names if you need) so our infra team can produce a proposed redaction profile? Preferably a single endpoint per file, ~50-200 lines. (Attachment accepted: carebridge-sample-logs.txt)
2) Please confirm residency requirement (you said us-west-2) and whether any EU residency constraints apply for other customers.
3) If helpful, we'll share a short draft redaction spec and a one-hour tech deep-dive with engineering.

Planned owner & timeline
- Grace (me): coordinate receipt of sample logs and schedule deep-dive.
- Ben (engineering): deliver a draft redaction-spec and recommended config by EOD Friday if we get samples by Wednesday.
- Jonas (security): will provide audit log proof options and the compliance checklist.

If the above matches what you expect, I’ll open a Drive folder and you can drop the sample logs there or reply to this thread.

Thanks —

- Retention: 30 days is fine for most traffic; highest-sensitivity endpoints should be 7 days. We'll flag those endpoints in the sample.
- Trace IDs: we cannot expose raw trace IDs to vendors, hashing is acceptable provided the salt is rotated and retained only in our KMS.

2) For auditability: we prefer redaction proofs (hash outputs for a subset) and a checksum-based proof that shows the scrubbing process ran without exposing raw data. Is that supported?

Amit —

Helpful notes — thank you. Short technical responses to your questions and a proposed approach:

1) Customer-supplied salt in KMS: yes, we can support using a customer-managed key (CMK) to derive the HMAC salt. Redwood will never persist the raw salt; we call the KMS during runtime to generate the HMAC key material. Rotation schedule: supportable but rotation requires re-hashing historical artifacts if you want historical linkage; otherwise newly generated hashes will use the new salt and we can tag them with a salt-version header.

2) Redaction proofs / checksums: we can provide deterministic proof artifacts — an auditable checksum log that shows inputs hashed and the hash outputs for a nonce subset (no raw data). We also offer a processing attest log (time-stamped) for each scrub pipeline run.

3) Implementation options (tradeoffs):
- Suppression: fastest, removes values entirely (no correlation possible).
- Deterministic HMAC (customer salt): allows correlation across requests without exposing PII; slightly higher CPU cost at ingest.
- Tokenization with reference store: allows reversible mapping for your team only, but requires you to host the token store or us to host it behind customer-managed keys.

4) Trace-ID handling: we'll implement a middleware that either strips the header or replaces the value with HMAC(trace-id || salt) and set a header redaction-version. That lets your tools correlate while keeping raw trace IDs out of our logs.

I've uploaded a short draft redaction specification for your review: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c-redaction-draft (redaction-specs-draft.pdf). If you prefer, I can also attach the PDF to this thread.

Next steps
- Grace: once we have the samples, Ben will produce a redaction profile and sample processed outputs (with proofs) by Friday EOD.
- Jonas: will prepare the compliance checklist items (SOC2 artifacts and where to find them on request).
- Proposed deep-dive: Thursday 2028-06-10, 10:00–11:00 PT. Grace, can you confirm?
